title: Laser Guide Star sweeps across a starry sky
caption: Laser guide star beam sweeping across the sky, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A powerful laser beam from ESO's Very Large Telescope fans out across the night sky over the Atacama Desert in this image by Julien Girard. The fan comes from the Earth's rotation during the 30-minute exposure and the laser moving to follow it. The same motion stretches the stars into curved trails, which shows their slightly different colours.

The beam makes sodium atoms 90 kilometres up glow, creating an artificial star. Measuring it lets astronomers correct for the atmosphere's blurring, a technique called adaptive optics. Bright natural stars can also serve, but a laser guide star can be placed wherever it is needed, so the technique works across more of the sky.

In the frame, the big enclosures of all four 8.2-metre Unit Telescopes appear, with the smaller VLT Survey Telescope behind. Moving enclosures appear blurred, and faint streaks of light were left by people walking across the platform.

understand.summary: This is a 30-minute exposure taken from a camera on a fixed tripod at ESO's Paranal Observatory, in visible light. Other camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points and a laser as a single thin line; only the long exposure spreads the beam into a fan and the stars into trails.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Girard is an ESO astronomer who works at the VLT. That night he was helping with observations on the Unit Telescope furthest to the right, so he set his camera on a fixed tripod before heading back to the control building.
He shared the picture through the Your ESO Pictures Flickr group, which ESO reviews for its Picture of the Week series.
alt: A laser beam fanning out across a sky of curved star trails above four large telescope enclosures.
